# Handoff to forever-addon-dev — measured client facts, 2026-09-20

Second outbound leg of the bridge described in the root README, and the consolidated one
promised by `pending-forever-addon-dev.md`. It supersedes that file, which is now closed.

Everything below was measured in a live client by **this** repo and is offered to the plugin
repo to record. Nothing here has been written into `forever-addon-dev`; classification and
placement belong to a session in that repo working under its own role and authority.

**Do not edit this file to reflect what was recorded.** It is a snapshot of what was handed
over. If a finding is rejected or reworded there, that repo's copy is authoritative.

**Item 1 is the one that matters.** It closes a caveat §P.22 states explicitly, and everything
else is an extension or a usage note.

## 1. `SetCVar` on the video CVars is permitted **in combat** — closes §P.22's stated caveat

§P.22 records the video CVars as writable and explicitly leaves combat unmeasured, noting this
fork's gating is not retail's — it allows `SecureActionButton:SetAttribute` in combat and
forbids `UseAction` out of it, so the usual reasoning does not transfer. It does here.

The same instrument was run once out of combat and once mid-fight, one pull apart:

| | out of combat | **in combat** |
|---|---|---|
| `InCombatLockdown()` | nil | **true** |
| `SetCVar` calls | 1618 over 3.00 s | **1742 over 3.00 s** |
| `Brightness` write → readback | 57 → 57 | **57 → 57** |
| `Contrast` write → readback | 57 → 57 | **57 → 57** |
| Restored afterwards | 50 / 50 | **50 / 50** |
| `isLockedFromUser` / `isSecure` / `isReadOnly` | false / false / false | **false / false / false** |
| `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` / `FORBIDDEN` | none | **none** |
| Frames | 809 in 3.00 s (270 fps) | 871 in 3.00 s (290 fps) |
| Frame gap max | 10 ms | **9 ms** |

Indistinguishable on every axis. Note the refusal count is a **captured event count**, not a
`pcall` result: this repo follows the plugin's own rule that a block here frequently fires
`ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED`/`FORBIDDEN` and returns normally, so both were registered for the
duration of each run and came back empty.

Suggested framing: §P.22 can drop its "run it again in combat for the other half" caveat, and
the `graphics-cvars-writable` restriction entry can state combat explicitly rather than being
silent on it.

Confidence: **high** — direct measurement, both states, same instrument, same session.
Not verified: whether this extends to CVars other than `Brightness` and `Contrast`, or to
instanced combat rather than open world.

## 2. `SetCVar` allocates ~822 bytes per call — corrects §P.22's framing

§P.22 concluded a write is "a cheap live post-process" on the evidence that 442 writes over
4 s produced no frame-gap spike. That is true and remains true *for frame time*. It is false
for allocation.

| Call | bytes per call |
|---|---|
| `C_CVar.SetCVar(name, "50.00")` | **822** |
| `C_CVar.SetCVar(name, 50.0)` — numeric | **827** |
| `("%.2f"):format(v)` alone, varying `v` | 38 |

Passing a number instead of a preformatted string does **not** avoid it: 827 vs 822. The
conversion happens internally and allocates regardless. The Lua-side format string accounts
for only 38 B, so `SetCVar` itself is responsible for ~784 B.

Consequence for any addon driving a CVar from `OnUpdate`: at a measured ~35 writes/s this is
~28 KB/s, ~99 MB/hour **per CVar driven**. Cheap in CPU (0.79 µs/call) and expensive in
garbage. The two costs point in opposite directions and an author reading only §P.22 will get
this wrong.

Suggested framing: keep §P.22's frame-time finding, add the allocation cost beside it, and
note explicitly that the numeric and string forms cost the same.

Confidence: **high** — collector stopped, 2000 calls, on `Brightness`.
Not verified: whether the figure differs per CVar, or for a CVar the client persists
differently. Only `Brightness` was measured.

## 3. `UnitPosition` is present and allocates nothing

`UnitPosition("player")` exists on this client and returns plain numbers.

| Call | bytes | µs |
|---|---|---|
| `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition` | 1864 | 4.38 – 5.71 |
| `UnitPosition` | **0.0** | not separately benched |

For any addon that polls player position this is strictly better on the allocation axis. The
tradeoff is coordinate space, not cost: `UnitPosition` returns world coordinates,
`GetPlayerMapPosition` normalized 0–1 map coordinates. Worth recording as a paired entry so
the next author sees both.

Confidence: **high** on presence and on the zero allocation.
Not verified: return-value order and units on this client (retail is `y, x, z, instanceID`);
behaviour in instances; whether it is restricted in combat. Only the allocation was measured.

## 4. `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition` returns an object with `GetXY`, and works indoors

Two parts, both measured.

**Shape.** Every run recorded `posShape = "object with GetXY (allocates)"`. That is where its
1864 B/call come from, and an addon that assumes two plain numbers gets nil for its `y`.

**Indoors.** Called inside the Northshire chapel it returns an ordinary point on the **parent**
map — `0.4905, 0.4096` on uiMapID 1429, with `GetBestMapForUnit` still returning 1429. It does
not go nil and the map does not change. This is worth recording beside the known retail caveat
that it returns nothing in instances: a building interior in the open world is not that case.

Confidence: **high** — shape across five runs, indoor behaviour across three captures.
Not verified: instances, and buildings that are their own map (a capital city inn, say).

## 5. `IsIndoors()` and `IsOutdoors()` are present, and disagree with `GetSubZoneText()` at the door

`IsIndoors()` / `IsOutdoors()` exist and return correct, complementary booleans.

**The trap, and it cost this repo a bug.** On the Northshire chapel stairway the client reports
`IsIndoors() == true` while `GetSubZoneText()` still returns the *outdoor* subzone
`Northshire Valley`. The two signals disagree across a band, not at a line. An addon that
treats the subzone name as authoritative for indoor/outdoor state will flip its behaviour
part-way through a building.

Observed sequence walking in and out, one line per change:

```
Northshire Valley                    outdoors
Northshire Valley  [indoors]         on the steps - the disagreement
Main Hall          [indoors]
Hall of Arms       [indoors]
Library Wing       [indoors]
Main Hall          [indoors]
Northshire Valley  [indoors]         on the way out, again
Northshire Valley                    outdoors
```

Also worth noting for the same class of addon: **subzone names are reported outdoors too**, so
a name alone cannot mean "inside". And a building shares its x,y with the ground it stands on,
so a map coordinate cannot express "indoors" either — `IsIndoors()` is the only signal that
carries it.

Suggested framing: a guides note for anyone doing location work, rather than a restriction —
nothing is forbidden here, it is just easy to get wrong.

Confidence: **high** — walked repeatedly, logged on change, reproduced in both directions.
Not verified: whether the disagreement band exists at every building or is specific to this
one's stairway geometry.

## 6. SavedVariables flush semantics — a usage note on the existing restriction

The plugin repo already records that SavedVariables are written but never read back. The
operational consequence is sharper than that phrasing suggests and cost a dataset here:

- The addon's saved table starts **nil** every session, because nothing is read back.
- A reload or logout writes **whatever the current session built**, and **replaces** the file
  rather than merging into it.
- So a reload *before* running anything writes an empty table over the previous session's
  results and destroys them. Only a reload *after* running saves anything.
- The client's own `.bak` beside the file is the only recovery, and it survives exactly one
  further flush.

On 2026-09-18 this silently destroyed five completed measurement runs. Recovered from `.bak`
only because it had not yet been overwritten a second time.

Suggested framing: a usage note on the existing restriction — "collect, then reload; never
reload first" — plus the `.bak` single-generation warning.

Confidence: **high** — observed directly, with file sizes and timestamps.

## 7. The runtime is the plain Lua 5.1 interpreter, not LuaJIT

Load-bearing rather than incidental: the allocation guard behind every byte figure in items 2
and 3 is only correct on a plain interpreter.

| Signal | Value |
|---|---|
| `_VERSION` | `Lua 5.1` |
| `jit` table | absent |
| `ffi`, `table.new`, `string.buffer` | absent |
| `bit` | present |

Two notes for whoever records this:

- **`_VERSION` alone does not answer the question.** LuaJIT also reports `Lua 5.1`. Anything
  distinguishing the two has to test for the `jit` table or LuaJIT-only globals.
- **`bit` is not evidence either way.** LuaJIT ships a `bit` library, but so does stock WoW. It
  discriminates nothing, and including it in a marker list produces a false "this is a JIT VM"
  — it did exactly that here before the list was corrected.

Why it matters: on a JIT VM, non-escaping allocations can be optimised away entirely and
`collectgarbage("stop")` does not reliably hold the collector. Both were observed under LuaJIT
2.1 while testing the guard, and either would silently invalidate a memory measurement.

Confidence: **high** — read from the live client, five signals agreeing.
Not verified: whether this holds across other builds of the same fork.

## 8. `collectgarbage("stop")` / `("restart")` behave as Lua 5.1 documents

The collector genuinely halts, which is what makes a byte-accurate allocation measurement
possible. Without stopping it, a collection inside the sample loop reads as a negative delta
and an allocating call reports as free.

Confidence: **high**, implied by every allocation figure above being stable and repeatable.

## 9. Two CVars written every frame at 290 fps still produce no hitch — extends §P.22

The frame-time half of item 1's two runs. §P.22's ramp drove **one** CVar for four seconds at
111 writes/s. This drove **both** `Brightness` and `Contrast` from `OnUpdate`, every frame:

| | |
|---|---|
| Frames | 809 in 3.00 s (270 fps) / 871 in 3.00 s (290 fps) |
| `SetCVar` calls | 1618 / 1742 — 539 and 581 per second |
| Frame gap | min 2 / p50 3–4 / p99 5 / **max 9–10 ms** |

Five times §P.22's write rate and more than twice its frame rate, worst single frame 10 ms.
The frame-time half of §P.22 holds and can be stated more strongly.

Confidence: **high** for the gap distribution. Note the same 1 ms `OnUpdate` granularity the
first handoff records, so these gaps are coarse — they can show a hitch, not size it.

## A lead, explicitly **not** a finding: the sweep may have cost frame rate

`GetFramerate` read 362.5 fps immediately before the first sweep; that sweep averaged 270. The
second run repeated the pattern but not the size: 321.7 before, 290 during — a 32 fps drop
where the first was 92, for identical work. A fixed per-write cost would not do that, which is
itself evidence against the hypothesis. If the first gap were the workload it would be
~0.95 ms per frame for two writes, three orders of magnitude above the measured 0.79 µs/call.

**Do not record this.** It is exactly the confound that got this repo's frame-gap phase data
excluded from the first handoff: one sample, one ordering, no warm-up discard, no control. It
is written down only because it is cheap to settle properly — an A-B-A of idle / one CVar per
frame / two CVars per frame, each with a warm-up discard — and because if there *is* a real
per-write frame cost at high frame rates, every addon driving a CVar from `OnUpdate` wants to
know.

## Minor, and the reference already has it right

There is **no global `GetCVarInfo`** on this build; it is `C_CVar.GetCVarInfo`, with the
documented seven-value shape. The generated reference is already correct — this note exists
only because a retail-shaped addon reaches for the global, gets nil, and silently skips its
lock-flag check rather than erroring. Possibly worth a line in `reference/guides/pitfalls.md`
alongside the other retail-idiom traps. No change to the API data is implied.

## Deliberately not sent

- **Area-evaluation cost** (0.17 µs per area, perfectly linear 10→500, zero allocation). This
  is our own Lua arithmetic, not client behaviour. Lives in this repo's README.
- **Frame-gap phase data** from `AmbianceCostDB.runs[*].phases`. Confounded by drift and a
  missing warm-up discard; excluded from the first handoff for the same reason.
- **String interning as a benchmarking trap** — formatting the same value repeatedly measures
  nothing because Lua interns the result, so an allocating call reports zero. A Lua fact, not a
  client fact.
- **Game data**: that Elwynn Forest is uiMapID 1429 here rather than retail's 37, and that the
  Northshire chapel is three subzones (`Main Hall`, `Hall of Arms`, `Library Wing`) rather than
  one called `Northshire Abbey`. Both cost this repo a wrong guess, but they are content, not
  client behaviour, and the plugin repo is addon-agnostic.

## Claims made in passing that turned out to be assertions

Kept because writing them down is what caused the wrong ones to be caught.

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| The write is the expensive call | **Wrong.** The position read is 6x more. Measured. |
| `GetPlayerMapPosition` is the dominant allocation | **Wrong.** `SetCVar` is, at ~35 writes/s. Measured. |
| A realistic write rate is 47/s | **Fabricated.** Back-fitted from the wrong fps. Measured: ~35/s. Caught by audit. |
| The epsilon skip throttles writes at high frame rates | **Wrong.** Absolute rate is flat ~35/s from 119 to 238 fps. |
| Passing a number to `SetCVar` avoids the string allocation | **Wrong.** 827 vs 822 bytes. Measured. |
| Formatting cost is negligible | **Unmeasurable as first written** — string interning hid it. Re-measured at 38 B. |
| WoW ships the Lua 5.1 interpreter, not LuaJIT | **Right, and now measured.** Item 7. |
| A block in combat is unlikely, since nothing carries lock flags | **Right, and now measured.** Item 1. It was still an assertion until it was run. |
| The chapel is one subzone called Northshire Abbey | **Wrong.** Three, and none of them that. Measured by walking it. |

## Open, and would strengthen a third handoff

- Whether item 1's in-combat result extends to CVars other than `Brightness` and `Contrast`,
  and to instanced combat rather than open world.
- Whether `SetCVar`'s ~822 B is constant across CVars or specific to `Brightness`.
- `UnitPosition`'s return order, units, and combat/instance availability.
- Whether a per-frame CVar write has a real frame-rate cost at high frame rates — the lead
  above, which needs an A-B-A with a warm-up discard rather than a single sample.
- Whether `useMaxFPS` and friends (first handoff, §1) are *writable* from an addon. Only reads
  were done, and that entry carries the caveat.
